title: Match: A Maximum-Likelihood Approach for Classification under Label Shift

problem.claim: Classifier performance can degrade when class distributions differ between training and deployment, a condition known as label shift.

gap.claim: Existing classifier-adjustment approaches, including instance re-weighting retraining and the Bayes update rule, do not ensure precise alignment with prevalence estimates from quantifiers.

contributions.claim: Introduces Match, an adjustment approach that maximizes the likelihood of predicted probabilities under class-prevalence constraints.
Formulates the adjustment process as a binary integer linear optimization problem solvable with mixed-integer optimization solvers.
Ensures that the adjusted class distribution aligns precisely with prevalence estimates from quantifiers.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe Match as a novel adjustment approach for classification under label shift.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Extensive experiments reportedly show that Match outperforms the state of the art in classifier adjustment with statistical significance.
The reported advantage is particularly pronounced for scenarios with imbalanced distributions.

narrative_sequence.summary: Label shift can cause classifier performance degradation when class distributions differ from the training distribution.
Match adjusts predicted probabilities by maximizing likelihood under class-prevalence constraints.
The approach is distinguished from existing adjustment methods by precisely aligning adjusted class distributions with quantifier prevalence estimates.
The adjustment is formulated as a binary integer linear optimization problem using mixed-integer solvers.
Experiments report statistically significant improvements over the state of the art, especially under imbalanced distributions.

source_observation.claim: The method constrains adjusted class distributions to match prevalence estimates from quantifiers.

interpretation.claim: Explicit prevalence constraints may help preserve target-distribution consistency during classifier adjustment.

application.claim: Consider constraint-based adjustment when deployment class prevalences are estimated separately from classifier predictions.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the accuracy or reliability requirements of the prevalence estimates.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, or effect sizes.
The abstract does not describe the assumptions, computational costs, or scalability limits of the optimization formulation.
